display.title: Episode 530: Never Too Late, Rabbi Akiva and the Whispering Droplets
display.summary_short: Counting the Omer teaches that time is precious; then how forty-year-old Akiva, inspired by drops of water wearing through a rock, began to learn Torah, and how to turn your house into a mitzvah.
display.summary_long: In the middle of Sefiras HaOmer, Uncle Yossi explains that we count days because every day is precious and should be better than the one before. A little girl keeps crying over a lost dime, no matter how many new dimes her mother gives her, which teaches us not to waste the time Hashem gives us now. After a boy recites the Shema in Studio 604 and everyone gives tzedakah, story time brings 'Never Too Late'. Akiva's devoted wife Rachel asks only one thing of him: that he learn Torah. At forty he thinks it is too late, until by a river he sees soft drops of water that have worn a hole through a hard rock. If water can do that, the words of Torah can enter his heart too. He goes off to learn and becomes the great Rabbi Akiva, who tells his thousands of students that all his honor belongs to Rachel. After a sponsor message and Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery, Uncle Yossi gives a mitzvah mission: fasten your tzedakah pushka to the wall so your whole house becomes part of a great mitzvah. The show closes with candle times and a reminder that this Shabbos we finish Sefer Vayikra with 'Chazak'.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift, so use every day for Torah and mitzvos; it is never too late to start learning.
